    def where(input, property, value)
      return input if !property || value.is_a?(Array) || value.is_a?(Hash)
      return input unless input.respond_to?(:select)

      input    = input.values if input.is_a?(Hash)
      input_id = input.hash

      # implement a hash based on method parameters to cache the end-result
      # for given parameters.
      @where_filter_cache ||= {}
      @where_filter_cache[input_id] ||= {}
      @where_filter_cache[input_id][property] ||= {}

      # stash or retrive results to return
      @where_filter_cache[input_id][property][value] ||= begin
        input.select do |object|
          compare_property_vs_target(item_property(object, property), value)
        end.to_a
      end
    end

    # Filters an array of objects against an expression
    #
    # input - the object array
    # variable - the variable to assign each item to in the expression
    # expression - a Liquid comparison expression passed in as a string
    #
    # Returns the filtered array of objects
    def where_exp(input, variable, expression)
      return input unless input.respond_to?(:select)

      input = input.values if input.is_a?(Hash) # FIXME

      expression = Jekyll::Filters.prepare_where_expression(variable, expression)
      condition = parse_condition(expression)
      @context.stack do
        input.select do |object|
          @context[variable] = object
          condition.evaluate(@context)
        end
      end || []
    end

    # Convert the input into integer
    #
    # input - the object string
    #
    # Returns the integer value
    def to_integer(input)
      return 1 if input == true
      return 0 if input == false

      input.to_i
    end

    # Sort an array of objects
    #
    # input - the object array
    # property - property within each object to filter by
    # nils ('first' | 'last') - nils appear before or after non-nil values
    #
    # Returns the filtered array of objects
    def sort(input, property = nil, nils = "first")
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot sort a null object." if input.nil?

      if property.nil?
        input.sort
      else
        if nils == "first"
          order = - 1
        elsif nils == "last"
          order = + 1
        else
          raise ArgumentError, "Invalid nils order: " \
            "'#{nils}' is not a valid nils order. It must be 'first' or 'last'."
        end

        sort_input(input, property, order)
      end
    end

    def pop(array, num = 1)
      return array unless array.is_a?(Array)

      num = Liquid::Utils.to_integer(num)
      new_ary = array.dup
      new_ary.pop(num)
      new_ary
    end

    def push(array, input)
      return array unless array.is_a?(Array)

      new_ary = array.dup
      new_ary.push(input)
      new_ary
    end

          def prepare_kramdown_config(config, highlighter_name)
          prepared = config
          prepared["syntax_highlighter"] ||= highlighter_name
          prepared["syntax_highlighter_opts"] ||= {}
          prepared["syntax_highlighter_opts"]["guess_lang"] = prepared["guess_lang"]
          prepared["coderay"] ||= {}
          modernize_kramdown_coderay(prepared)
          prepared
          end
          def modernize_kramdown_coderay(config)
          coderay_config = config["coderay"]
          return config if coderay_config.nil? || coderay_config.empty?
          Jekyll::Deprecator.deprecation_message(
            "You are using 'kramdown.coderay' in your configuration, please use 'syntax_highlighter_opts' instead."
          )
          config["syntax_highlighter_opts"] = strip_coderay_prefix(
            config["syntax_highlighter_opts"].merge(CODERAY_HIGHLIGHTER_DEFAULTS).merge(coderay_config)
          )
          config
          end
          def strip_coderay_prefix(hash)
          hash.each_with_object({}) do |(key, val), hsh|
            cleaned_key = key.to_s.gsub(%r!\Acoderay_!, "")
            Jekyll::Deprecator.deprecation_message("You are using '#{key}'. Normalizing to #{cleaned_key}.") if key != cleaned_key
            hsh[cleaned_key] = val
          end
          end
          def prepare_where_expression(variable, expression)
          remember_filter_variable(variable)
          intern_condition_expression(expression)
          end
          def remember_filter_variable(variable)
          @filter_variable_names ||= {}
          name = variable.to_s
          @filter_variable_names[name] = name
          name
          end
          def intern_condition_expression(expression)

          @filter_expression_interns ||= {}
          @filter_expression_interns[source] ||= begin
            tokens = tokenize_filter_expression(source)
            run_expression_analyzers(source, tokens)
            source
          end
          end
          def tokenize_filter_expression(source)
          tokens = []
          index = 0
          while index < source.length
            kind = classify_expression_char(source[index])
            token, consumed = read_expression_token(source, index, kind)
            tokens << token
            index += consumed
          end
          tokens
          end
          def classify_expression_char(char)
          return :blank if char.nil? || char.empty?
          code = char.ord
          if char == " " || char == "\t" || char == "\n" || char == "\r"
            :space
          elsif char == "'" || char == '"'
            :quote
          elsif code.between?(48, 57)
            :digit
          elsif code.between?(65, 90) || code.between?(97, 122) || char == "_"
            :ident
          elsif %w(= ! < >).include?(char)
            :operator
          else

          end
          end
          def read_expression_token(source, index, kind)
          if kind == :space
            read_while_kind(source, index, :space, "space")
          elsif kind == :quote
            read_expression_string(source, index)
          elsif kind == :digit
            read_while_kind(source, index, :digit, "number")

            read_expression_operator(source, index)

`parse_binary_comparison` now parses chained `and`/`or` operators recursively instead of stopping after one, so `where_exp` supports unlimited conditions.

Validation:
- All 12 `where_exp` tests pass, including the new multi-condition case.
- All 7 `group_by_exp` tests pass.
- Full `test_filters.rb` has only 2 pre-existing Ruby 3.3 keyword-argument errors in unrelated `jsonify` tests.
